sample.title: Sample talk: How the internet works
sample.transcript: Welcome. In this short sample talk, we look at how the internet works, from typing an address to seeing a page. First, your computer needs to find the server that holds the website. It asks a system called DNS, the domain name system, which works like a phone book. You give it a name such as example dot com, and it replies with a number called an IP address. Second, your browser opens a connection to that address. Data does not travel as one big block. It is cut into small pieces called packets, and each packet can take a different route across many routers before it arrives. At the other end, the pieces are put back in the right order. Third, the browser and the server agree on rules for talking, called a protocol. The web uses HTTP, and the secure version, HTTPS, adds encryption so that nobody in the middle can read what is sent. This is why you see a padlock in the address bar. Fourth, the server sends back files: HTML for the structure of the page, CSS for the style, and JavaScript for behaviour. Your browser reads them and draws the page on your screen. Finally, remember three ideas. Names are turned into numbers by DNS. Data travels in packets. And HTTPS keeps the conversation private. If you want to practise, open your browser's developer tools, go to the network tab, and reload any page. You will see every request the browser makes, one by one. Thanks for watching this sample.
